title: Good Times
statementMd:
A time of day is represented by three integers: hours, minutes, and seconds. A time is called good if one of these integers equals the sum of the other two.

Given two times on the same day in the 24-hour format, count the good times between them, including both endpoints.

## Input

There is only one test case in each test file.

The first line contains three integers $h_1$, $m_1$, and $s_1$ ($0\le h_1\le23$, $0\le m_1,s_1\le59$), representing the hours, minutes, and seconds of the starting time, respectively.

The second line contains three integers $h_2$, $m_2$, and $s_2$ ($0\le h_2\le23$, $0\le m_2,s_2\le59$), representing the hours, minutes, and seconds of the ending time, respectively.

It is guaranteed that the starting time is no later than the ending time.

## Output

Print one integer: the number of good times.

## Note

In the first example, the only good time is $00{:}02{:}02$, since $0+2=2$, so the answer is $1$.

In the second example, the good times are $01{:}45{:}46$ and $01{:}46{:}45$, so the answer is $2$.
